what: Agree Realty buys single-tenant retail properties and leases them to large chains on long leases: Walmart, Tractor Supply, Dollar General, TJX, O'Reilly and similar.
customers: Investment-grade retail chains, which sign leases of ten to twenty years.
money: net lease rent from retail properties
moat: A portfolio weighted toward tenants with investment-grade credit, which makes the rent unusually safe compared with the discount retailers other net-lease REITs rely on.
risks: Free cash flow is deeply negative because the company is buying property faster than it earns
36 times earnings for a landlord growing rents by about 1% a year contractually
Rising interest rates raise the cost of the capital it needs to keep buying
opportunities: Revenue grew from $353M to $738M in four years with a 27.7% net margin
Analysts see about 11% upside, with 18 covering the stock
The dividend is paid monthly and has been raised consistently, which draws income investors
watch: Acquisition volume and the cap rate at which new properties are bought.
